claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated at the White House that direct talks with Iran would begin within a day or two.
Donald Trump said of negotiations with Iran, "They’re going to go quickly one way or the other. It’s not very complex."
Donald Trump outlined a two-phase plan where phase one is opening the Strait of Hormuz and phase two is denuclearisation.
Trump called off threatened military strikes against Iran for the 12th time during the war after Gulf allies urged diplomacy.
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei denied that Iran is currently holding any direct talks with the United States.
Esmaeil Baghaei stated that Iran is negotiating with Oman to establish an acceptable shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz.
Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social calling Iranian leadership "unbelievably duplicitous" after Tehran denied holding talks.
US President Donald Trump stated that Iran has a "last chance" to reach a nuclear agreement.
Global oil prices fell following Trump's announcement, with Brent Crude dropping 4.5% to $83.98 and US-traded oil dropping 4.6% to $80.74.
Approximately 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas normally flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
According to Kpler data, commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz dropped by 28% to 51 vessel crossings between July 30 and August 2.
US Vice-President JD Vance previously led face-to-face peace negotiations with Iran in Pakistan following warnings by Trump in April.
The armed conflict between the United States and Iran began on February 28, 2026, following US and Israeli strikes on Iranian targets.
Migrants awaiting asylum on a beach in Ceuta, Spain, rushed to receive water and beverages.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged strengthening EU external borders in a letter to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
Spanish authorities began installing a 500-metre floating barrier at the border with Morocco near Ceuta.
Spain estimated that approximately 69,500 migrants returned to Morocco over four days following arrivals in Ceuta.
Authorities in Ceuta reported 88 migrant deaths trying to reach the territory, while Morocco recorded at least 11 deaths.
Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish enclaves in North Africa representing the European Union's only land borders with Africa.
Leaders of 22 EU member states signed a letter urging effective deterrence against illegal migration and criticizing large-scale regularisations.
Italy temporarily suspended passport-free Schengen travel arrangements with Spain for one month following the Ceuta border surge.
Ceuta official Juan Jesus Vivas estimated that between 3,000 and 5,000 migrants remained in the city of Ceuta.
France announced temporary border checks in response to the migrant influx into Ceuta.
The Moroccan Association for Human Rights reported nearly 130 people died or went missing during the Ceuta border crossings.
Wildfires west of Athens jumped containment lines near Megara, forcing the evacuation of over 1,000 people from Porto Germeno.
Two private helicopter crew members, a Greek national and a Danish national, died in a midair collision during Greek firefighting operations.
According to the UK Met Office, England and Wales recorded their driest July in nearly 200 years of recordkeeping.
Two contractors were arrested in Greece on charges of negligent arson linked to a faulty wind farm power line.
The Romanian military detonated a rocky outcrop in the Danube riverbed to increase cooling water flow to the Cernavoda nuclear power plant.
Carmakers Dacia and Ford agreed to suspend production in Romania until August 19 to reduce electricity consumption.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant operated at little more than 10% capacity due to low Danube water levels.
Serbia's Iron Gate hydroelectric plant operated at approximately one-fifth of its capacity due to low river levels.
Navigable water depth at the Kaub chokepoint on the Rhine River dropped to 25cm, matching a record low set in 2018.
Romania's military blasted part of the Danube riverbed to redirect water towards the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant.
A Ukrainian drone strike on a beach in Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik killed seven people, including three children, and injured 40 others.
Krasnodar Krai Governor Veniamin Kondratyev accused Ukraine of a deliberate attack on civilians.
Russia's health ministry reported 21 people were hospitalized following the Gelendzhik beach explosion, with nine in serious condition.
Eyewitnesses reported hearing machine-gun fire before the drone exploded on the beach, indicating Russian air defences attempted to intercept it.
A Ukrainian drone strike hit a Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Vladimir region overnight.
Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv killed at least nine people and injured dozens on Saturday.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova accused NATO and the EU of sponsoring international terrorist activity following the beach strike.
Russian anti-war politician Boris Nadezhdin fled Russia and arrived in Paris, France.
Russia's justice ministry designated Boris Nadezhdin a "foreign agent" in July 2026.
Nadezhdin was barred from running in Russia's September 2026 parliamentary elections due to a foreign agent label and an extremism charge.
Nadezhdin was barred from Russia's 2024 presidential election after election officials claimed over 15% of his candidate signatures were flawed.
Nadezhdin was charged in Russia with displaying extremist symbols for featuring a 10-second image of Alexei Navalny in a reposted video.
Russian President Vladimir Putin secured a fifth term in office following the March 18, 2024 presidential election.
Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor won the Bankipur Assembly by-election in Bihar, defeating BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha by 19,324 votes.
Prashant Kishor received 64,151 votes in Bankipur, while BJP's Neeraj Kumar Sinha received 44,827 votes and RJD's Rekha Kumari received 14,273 votes.
The Bankipur seat was previously held for five consecutive terms by Nitin Nabin before his election to the Rajya Sabha.
In Gujarat's Manjalpur by-election, BJP candidate Satish Govindbhai Patel defeated Congress candidate Bhikhabhai Rabari by 30,630 votes.
In Madhya Pradesh's Datia by-election, Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeated BJP candidate Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes.
Independent candidates named Lalu Prasad and Nitish Kumar lost their security deposits in Bankipur, securing 81 and 149 votes respectively.
The BJP had held the Bankipur Assembly seat continuously since 1995.
Prashant Kishor stated that the public atmosphere generated by recent nationwide Gen Z protests may have contributed to his win in Bankipur.
BJP national president Nitin Nabin stated the party accepts the election outcome and will conduct a thorough introspection regarding defeats in Bankipur and Datia.
A New Delhi court acquitted former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in a sexual harassment and stalking case.
Complainant wrestler Vinesh Phogat stated that the female wrestlers will appeal the court's acquittal verdict as soon as possible.
In December 2023, Olympic wrestler Bajrang Punia returned a civilian award and Sakshi Malik retired from wrestling to protest Singh.
Delhi Police registered two FIRs against Singh in April 2023, including one under the POCSO Act based on allegations by a minor wrestler.
A Delhi court accepted a closure report cancelling the POCSO case against Singh in May 2025 after the minor complainant withdrew allegations.
A Delhi court framed charges of sexual harassment, outraging modesty, and criminal intimidation against Singh in May 2024.
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwini Panwar acquitted Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar at Rouse Avenue Courts.
The flood death toll in Assam rose to 87 after two additional deaths were reported in Sivasagar district.
More than 1.28 lakh people across seven districts in Assam remain affected by monsoon floods.
Monsoon rain-related incidents in Kerala killed 15 people and left seven others missing.
The Kerala government announced financial aid including Rs 8 lakh ex-gratia for families of the deceased and Rs 12 lakh for those losing homes to landslides.
Flooding displaced 11,018 people into 316 relief camps across Kerala.
The Ernakulam District Collector ordered all educational institutions closed on August 4 due to persistent heavy rainfall.
Water levels at Malankara dam in Ernakulam district reached the red-alert mark of 41.30 metres.
In Kozhikode district, 964 people from 365 families were accommodated across 32 flood relief camps.
Authorities opened two spillway gates at Kakkayam Dam to release water into the Kuttiyadi River.
